frontier.hypothesis: The allocno-priority instrument (E-s23-3, floor_log2(n_refs)*n_refs/live_length read off .lreg's per-register header) closes register-identity-only residuals elsewhere in the queue without any spelling search.
frontier.mechanism: global.c's allocno_compare sorts allocnos by that priority, so splitting a C variable (fewer refs, shorter live range) lowers it and fusing uses raises it, moving find_reg's assignment order deterministically. Validated on this function: it predicted, on the first try, that splitting base into base1/base2 (10/22 -> 5/11) would drop below p (0.923) and hand p the $a0 it lacked, and cell S1's .greg confirmed it.
frontier.next_probe: On the next queue item whose sandbox residual is register identity only (same instruction kinds, same count, same order), dump .lreg, compute the priority table by hand, and predict the split/fuse that reorders the two conflicting allocnos before spending any sandbox run. It has no purchase on func_80017848 - that residual is two instruction KINDS, and no allocation order turns a lw into an addu.

frontier.hypothesis: grindlib.validate_outcome's file reads are a single-byte-fragile failure mode for the whole pipeline, not just for this function: any session that writes a cp1252 character into docs/grind/decisions.md discards itself and every later owner-gated session until someone repairs the file.
frontier.mechanism: grindlib.py:388 opens the file with encoding='utf-8' and no errors= policy, inside the owner-gated branch, before the OWNER-ESCALATION check; the exception escapes validate_outcome entirely rather than becoming a validation failure with a message.
frontier.next_probe: Operator-side (outside a grind session's allowed surface): either pass errors='replace' at grindlib.py:388 or wrap the read so a decode error becomes a named validation failure, and add a pre-commit check that docs/grind/*.md is valid UTF-8. Until then, sessions writing that file must emit ASCII or explicit UTF-8.
